plain_text:
A RECENT STUDY HAS
FOUND that a drug may
delay the start of type 1
diabetes in people who are
high risk, such as people who
have a family member with
the disease.
semantic_text: A RECENT STUDY HAS FOUND that a drug may delay the start of type 1 diabetes in people who are high risk, such as people who have a family member with the disease.

plain_text:
Type 1 diabetes is a serious
lifelong condition in which
the body makes little or no
insulin. Insulin is a hormone
that manages your blood
sugar to give you energy.
People with type 1 diabetes
have to take insulin every day
to stay alive.
semantic_text: Type 1 diabetes is a serious lifelong condition in which the body makes little or no insulin. Insulin is a hormone that manages your blood sugar to give you energy. People with type 1 diabetes have to take insulin every day to stay alive.

plain_text:
Type 1 diabetes is usually
diagnosed in kids and teens,
but it can develop at any age.
semantic_text: Type 1 diabetes is usually diagnosed in kids and teens, but it can develop at any age.

plain_text:
The National Institutes of
Health-supported clinical trial
followed 76 people at high
risk of developing type 1
diabetes. Half of the people
in the study were given
the drug, teplizumab, and
half took a placebo, which
doesn't have any medicine.
Researchers followed the
participants for several years.
semantic_text: The National Institutes of Health-supported clinical trial followed 76 people at high risk of developing type 1 diabetes. Half of the people in the study were given the drug, teplizumab, and half took a placebo, which doesn't have any medicine. Researchers followed the participants for several years.

plain_text:
Participants who took the
drug were diagnosed with
type 1 diabetes more than
two-and-a-half years later
than the placebo group. Also,
50% of the people treated
with the drug didn’t develop
the disease at all during the
study; 22% of the people in
the placebo group did not
develop it.
semantic_text: Participants who took the drug were diagnosed with type 1 diabetes more than two-and-a-half years later than the placebo group. Also, 50% of the people treated with the drug didn’t develop the disease at all during the study; 22% of the people in the placebo group did not develop it.

plain_text:
People who took the drug
also showed improved insulin
production.
semantic_text: People who took the drug also showed improved insulin production.

plain_text:
If it is approved, tepizumab
would be the first drug
to delay or even prevent
the development of type 1
diabetes. It has the potential
to offer significant benefits to
many people at risk for type 1
diabetes, especially “for those
children who might have a
chance to grow up without
it,
” according to study author
Kevan Herold, M.D.
semantic_text: If it is approved, tepizumab would be the first drug to delay or even prevent the development of type 1 diabetes. It has the potential to offer significant benefits to many people at risk for type 1 diabetes, especially “for those children who might have a chance to grow up without it, ” according to study author Kevan Herold, M.D.

plain_text:
EARLY DIAGNOSIS for cystic fibrosis (CF) can
make a big difference in improving the quality of life
for people with CF. It can also help them live longer.
That's why a recent study from the National Institutes
of Health is important to potentially providing an
earlier and more reliable diagnosis.
semantic_text: EARLY DIAGNOSIS for cystic fibrosis (CF) can make a big difference in improving the quality of life for people with CF. It can also help them live longer. That's why a recent study from the National Institutes of Health is important to potentially providing an earlier and more reliable diagnosis.

plain_text:
CF is a chronic genetic disorder that creates a
mucus buildup in the lungs and other organs. Usually,
CF is diagnosed with a sweat test, which measures the
amount of chloride in sweat. People with CF have high
levels of chloride in their sweat.
semantic_text: CF is a chronic genetic disorder that creates a mucus buildup in the lungs and other organs. Usually, CF is diagnosed with a sweat test, which measures the amount of chloride in sweat. People with CF have high levels of chloride in their sweat.

plain_text:
The current sweat test, which is most often done in
infants, uses a device strapped to the wrist to make a
child sweat. The sweat is collected for 30 minutes and
then measured.
semantic_text: The current sweat test, which is most often done in infants, uses a device strapped to the wrist to make a child sweat. The sweat is collected for 30 minutes and then measured.

plain_text:
But this approach often produces too little sweat

for a reliable measurement.
semantic_text:
But this approach often produces too little sweat

for a reliable measurement.

plain_text:
Now researchers have developed a wearable device
they've dubbed the "sweat sticker." It sticks to the skin
using an adhesive that's safe for newborn babies, since
that's often when children are tested for the condition.
semantic_text: Now researchers have developed a wearable device they've dubbed the "sweat sticker." It sticks to the skin using an adhesive that's safe for newborn babies, since that's often when children are tested for the condition.

plain_text:
Measuring only about 1 millimeter thick-about the
width of the point on a pencil—the sticker collected
33% more sweat on average than the current sweat
test in one study.
semantic_text: Measuring only about 1 millimeter thick-about the width of the point on a pencil—the sticker collected 33% more sweat on average than the current sweat test in one study.

plain_text:
More research is needed before the sticker can be
used in clinical settings. But it could make future cystic
fibrosis testing more reliable, especially in infants.
semantic_text: More research is needed before the sticker can be used in clinical settings. But it could make future cystic fibrosis testing more reliable, especially in infants.

Medical Sciences; National Institute on Aging
semantic_text: SOURCES: NIH Research Matters; National Institute of General Medical Sciences; National Institute on Aging

plain_text:
Children and adults with type 1 diabetes have to measure their blood
sugar multiple times a day.
